readerQuestion: What questions should I ask a financial advisor before hiring them? [PAA unavailable (SERP unread, no DataForSEO credentials); ac 18 of the 23 completions are on-topic (before hiring, first meeting, retirement, investing, interview, potential/prospective/new advisor); 5 are locale or brand variants (Australia, UK x2, Canada, Dave Ramsey)]

decisionGap: Readers asking this question cannot get the primary-source answer and its conditions on this site; the nearest pages answer a neighboring decision (see coverage.txt).
finding: The SEC requires every registered broker-dealer and investment adviser to print standard conversation-starter questions on its relationship summary; those questions cover service type, investment selection, qualifications, fees on a $10,000 example, legal obligations, conflicts, compensation and disciplinary history, so a reader can compare firms with one list.
conditions: Applies to registered investment advisers and broker-dealers serving US retail investors; insurance-only agents and banks may use other forms.
whatWouldChange: A revision to Form CRS or the SEC conversation-starter list.
method: Reported primary-source synthesis; no test or model.
whyNoQuantitativeAnalysis: The reader decision is definitional or procedural and rests on regulator and credential-body statements; no defensible numerical input exists, so arithmetic would only restate source figures.
reasoning: From the fetched primary pages listed in sources.md to the answer: The SEC requires every registered broker-dealer and investment adviser to print standard conversation-starter questions on its relationship summary; those questions cover service type, investment selection, qualifications, fees on a $10,000 example, legal obligations, conflicts, compensation and disciplinary history, so a reader can compare firms with one list.

takeawayPlan: Ask every candidate the same short list from the SEC relationship summary, then compare their written answers with their Form CRS and public record; walk away from anyone who is not registered; treat a missing Form CRS or a disciplinary record you cannot get explained as reasons to look elsewhere. Applies to anyone hiring an advisor or broker. Evidence basis: reported (SEC Form CRS as printed by a registered firm, Investor.gov). Changes if you need only a one-time answer. Next step: copy the list, send it before the first meeting and check the registration on Investor.gov.
